'''The Heights''' or '''Jersey City Heights''' is a neighborhood in [[Jersey City, New Jersey]], located atop the [[New Jersey Palisades]], along the west side of the [[Hudson River]]. It is bound by [[Paterson Plank Road]] on the north, [[Highway 139]] on the south, [[Hoboken, New Jersey|Hoboken]] on the east, and the [[Hackensack River]] on the west.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hobokengirl.com/jersey-city-heights-historical-walking-tour/|author=Gittleman, Nicole|title=A Historical Walking Tour of Jersey City Heights|publisher=The Hoboken Girl|language=en-US|url-status=live|date=January 10, 2023|access-date=January 19, 2023|archive-date=January 11, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230111171946/https://www.hobokengirl.com/jersey-city-heights-historical-walking-tour/}}</ref><ref name=CASIMC>{{cite web|url=https://jcheights.com/our-neighborhood/about-the-heights/|title=About the Heights|publisher=Central Avenue Special Improvement Management Corporation|language=en-US|url-status=live|access-date=January 19, 2023|archive-date=December 4, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221204005920/https://jcheights.com/our-neighborhood/about-the-heights/}}</ref> and Penhorn Creek on the west.<ref name=CASIMC/> Its postal area [[ZIP Code]]s are 07307, and portions of 07306.<ref name=CASIMC/>

==Neighborhoods and thoroughfares==
[[Central Avenue (Hudson County)|Central Avenue]] is one of Jersey City's 13 different neighborhood shopping districts.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.jerseycityonline.com/jersey_city_shopping_districts.htm|title=Jersey City Shopping Districts|language=en-US|url-status=live|date=2007|access-date=January 19, 2023|archive-date=January 19, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230119143636/http://www.jerseycityonline.com/jersey_city_shopping_districts.htm}}</ref> with more than 240 businesses serving the area.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.jcheights.com/community-aboutJCHeights.shtml|title=The Heights Section of Jersey City|publisher=Central Avenue Special Improvement District|language=en-US|url-status=live|access-date=March 10, 2019|archive-date=December 31, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191231172831/http://www.jcheights.com/community-aboutJCHeights.shtml}}</ref> [[Pershing Field]] (named for [[General Pershing|General John J Pershing]]) is a memorial park in the center of the district that was built on a military training ground. It offers a green space, baseball fields, a swimming pool and ice-skating rink. The adjacent [[Jersey City Reservoir No. 3]] has been preserved as a state designated wetland and park. Many stately [[Victorian architecture|Victorian]] and [[Edwardian period|Edwardian]] homes distinguish the Heights, particularly along [[Summit Avenue, Hudson County|Summit Avenue]] and Sherman Place.<ref name=GetNJ>{{cite web|author=Olszewski, Anthony|url=http://www.getnj.com/jerseycity/heights.shtml|title=The Heights Section of Jersey City|publisher=GET NJ|language=en-US|url-status=live|access-date=January 19, 2023|archive-date=January 19, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230119153130/http://www.getnj.com/jerseycity/heights.shtml}}</ref>

==Transportation==
An elevator at Congress Street and [[Paterson Plank Road]] descends to the [[9th Street-Congress Street (HBLR station)|9th Street-Congress Street]] station of the [[Hudson-Bergen Light Rail]].<ref name=GetNJ/> Mountain Ave<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.state.nj.us/transportation/refdata/sldiag/09000731__-.pdf|title=Hudson County 7311 straight line diagram|publisher=[[New Jersey Department of Transportation]]|access-date=August 14, 2021|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121017170551/http://www.state.nj.us/transportation/refdata/sldiag/09000731__-.pdf|archive-date=2012-10-17}}</ref> and New York Ave are among the streets that run through the area.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.state.nj.us/transportation/refdata/sldiag/09000671__-.pdf|title=Hudson County 6671 straight line diagram|publisher=[[New Jersey Department of Transportation]]|access-date=August 14, 2021}}</ref>

==History==
The Heights was part of the colony of [[Pavonia, New Netherland]], the superintendent of which was the American patriarch of the [[Van Vorst Park|Van Vorst]] family. A [[Van Vorst House]] built in 1742 by the family (now on Palisade Avenue) is considered to be the oldest building in [[Hudson County]]. [[Summit Avenue (Hudson County)|Summit Avenue]], slightly to the west follows an [[Hackensack (Native Americans)|Hackensack Indian]] trail that became the main road from the villages of [[Communipaw]] and [[Bergen Square|Bergen]] and eventually connected to the [[Paterson Plank Road|Paterson]] and [[Hackensack Plank Road]]s.<ref>{{cite web|last= Olszewski|first=Anthony|title=From Before the Revolutionary War! Jersey City's Oldest House|publisher=City of Jersey City|year=2002|url = http://www.cityofjerseycity.org/vanvorstfarmhouse.shtml|access-date=December 13, 2021|archive-date=May 2, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210502153830/http://www.cityofjerseycity.org/vanvorstfarmhouse.shtml}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title = 2012 Jersey City Historic Preservation Month|newspaper=[[The Jersey Journal]]|date = April 30, 2012|url = http://photos.nj.com/jersey-journal/2012/04/2012_jersey_city_historic_pres_2.html| access-date = December 13, 2021|archive-date=August 11, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140811172201/http://photos.nj.com/jersey-journal/2012/04/2012_jersey_city_historic_pres_2.html}}</ref>

E.R.V Wright was the first Mayor of Hudson City.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://query.nytimes.com/gst/abstract.html?res=9903E3D61F3EE334BC4152DFB266838E649FDE|title=NEW-JERSEY.; The City of Hudson.|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|date=April 19, 1885|accessdate=December 13, 2021|archive-date=December 13, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211213182448/https://www.nytimes.com/1855/04/19/archives/newjersey-the-city-of-hudson.html}}</ref>

[[File:Pathé Studio Scene—Director Handworth Posing a Military Drama.jpg|thumb|Filming at the [[Pathé]] American studio in Jersey City Heights (1912)]]
In the early 20th century, before [[Hollywood, Los Angeles|Hollywood]], the American motion picture industry was mainly based in New Jersey towns along the Hudson River.<ref name=NYTimes10.4.98>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/10/04/nyregion/getting-big-picture-film-industry-started-here-left-now-it-s-back-state-says.html|author=Kannapell, Andrea|title=Getting the Big Picture; The Film Industry Started Here and Left. Now It's Back, and the State Says the Sequel Is Huge.|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|language=en-US|url-status=live|date=October 4, 1998|access-date=January 19, 2023|archive-date=December 19, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191219034718/https://www.nytimes.com/1998/10/04/nyregion/getting-big-picture-film-industry-started-here-left-now-it-s-back-state-says.html}}</ref> Chief among them was [[Fort Lee, New Jersey|Fort Lee]], which was the [[Cinema of the United States#Origins and Fort Lee|nation's first motion picture capital]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://j-entonline.com/before-hollywood-there-was-fort-lee-n-j-early-movie-making-in-new-jersey-a-j-ent-dvd-review/|author=Amith, Dennis|title=Before Hollywood There Was Fort Lee, N.J.: Early Movie Making in New Jersey (a J!-ENT DVD Review)|publisher=J!-ENT|language=en-US|url-status=live|date=January 1, 2011|access-date=January 19, 2023|archive-date=December 22, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191222043615/http://j-entonline.com/blu-ray-dvd-reviews/dvd-reviews-film-tv/before-hollywood-there-was-fort-lee-n-j-early-movie-making-in-new-jersey-a-j-ent-dvd-review/}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nj.com/news/index.ssf/2012/04/100_years_ago_fort_lee_was_the.html|author=Rose, Lisa|title=100 years ago, Fort Lee was the first town to bask in movie magic|publisher=[[NJ.com]]|language=en-US|url-status=live|date=April 29, 2012|access-date=January 19, 2023|archive-date=September 29, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180929115649/https://www.nj.com/news/index.ssf/2012/04/100_years_ago_fort_lee_was_the.html}}</ref> with other early film studios headquartered in neighboring towns such as Jersey City.<ref name=NYTimes10.4.98/> Among those was a branch of the French company [[Pathé]], the largest film equipment and production company in the world, whose American factory and studio facility was in established in the Heights in 1910, in a building that still overlooks [[Paterson Plank Road]]. Pathé also established the subsidiary  Eclectic Film Company, as a distributor for both its American and European product. Although the Jersey City plant produced moderately popular comedies, dramas, and newsreels largely directed at the US market, ''[[The Perils of Pauline (1914 serial)|Perils of Pauline]]'' was the first American-made Pathé effort to achieve worldwide success under the Eclectic banner.<ref>{{Citation|last=Koszarski|first=Richard|title=Fort Lee: The Film Town|place=Rome, Italy|publisher=John Libbey Publishing - CIC srl|year=2004|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=5w0r8YKan04C&q=Fort+Lee:+the+film+town+Door+Richard+Koszarski|isbn=0-86196-653-8}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title = Studios and Films|publisher=Fort Lee Film Commission|url=http://www.fortleefilm.org/studios.html|access-date=May 30, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|last=Fort Lee Film Commission|title=Fort Lee Birthplace of the Motion Picture Industry|publisher=Arcadia Publishing|year=2006|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ViR3b72xkK0C&q=Fort+Lee+Birthplace+of+the+Motion+Picture+Industry|isbn=0-7385-4501-5}}</ref>

==Education==
[[Jersey City Public Schools]] operates public schools in the Heights.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nces.ed.gov/ccd/districtsearch/district_detail.asp?Search=2&details=1&ID2=3407830&DistrictID=3407830|title=Search for Public School Districts: District Detail for Jersey City Public Schools|publisher=[[National Center for Education Statistics]]|date=2020|accessdate=December 13, 2021|archive-date=May 15, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210515000650/https://nces.ed.gov/ccd/districtsearch/district_detail.asp?Search=2&details=1&ID2=3407830&DistrictID=3407830}}</ref>

The [[Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Newark]] operates area Catholic Schools. St. Anne School was located in Jersey City Heights, and opened in 1904.<ref name=Zeitlingeronce>{{cite web|author=Zeitlinger, Ron|url=https://www.nj.com/hudson/2011/05/once_doomed_st_annes_school_in.html|title=Once doomed, St. Anne's School in Jersey City gets new life|newspaper=[[The Jersey Journal]]|via=[[NJ.com]]|language=en-US|url-status=live|date=May 22, 2011|access-date=January 19, 2023|archive-date=June 26, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200626162705/https://www.nj.com/hudson/index.ssf/2011/05/once_doomed_st_annes_school_in.html}}</ref> Its enrollment declined by 33 in 2011<!--"last year"--> and increased by 22 in 2012. James Carroll, a member of the Jersey City Police Department and a member of the school board, Carroll stated that the 2011 decline was due to parents being afraid that the school would close.<ref name=ConteAnneDei>{{cite web|author=Conte, Michaelangelo|url=http://www.nj.com/hudson/index.ssf/2012/02/newark_archdiocese_to_close_st.html |title=Newark Archdiocese to close St. Anne's School in Jersey City, Mater Dei Academy in Kearny|newspaper=[[The Jersey Journal]]|date=2012-02-17|access-date=2020-06-24}}</ref> In 2011, the archdiocese considered closing the school, but a fundraising generated sufficient money to keep it open.<ref name=Zeitlingeronce/> It closed in 2012.<ref name=ConteAnneDei/> That year the building housed the K-8 grades of the [[Hoboken Charter School]] on a temporary basis as the regular K-8 building of the charter school was badly damaged by a fire.<ref>{{cite web|author=Thorbourne, Ken|url=https://www.nj.com/hobokennow/2012/09/fire-devastated_hoboken_charte.html|title=Fire-devastated Hoboken Charter School to reopen in Jersey City Heights|newspaper=[[The Jersey Journal]]|via=[[NJ.com]]|language=en-US|url-status=live|date=January 18, 2012|access-date=June 24, 2020|archive-date=June 24, 2020|archive-url=https://archive.today/20200624183527/https://www.nj.com/hobokennow/2012/09/fire-devastated_hoboken_charte.html}}</ref>
